subject: Biology
description: Light + dark reactions, chlorophyll, C3-C4-CAM, factors, products, exam-favourite distractors

questions.stem: The site of the LIGHT reactions of photosynthesis within a chloroplast is the:
questions.explanation: Chloroplast structure: outer + inner envelope; inside, the STROMA (fluid matrix) contains stacks of disc-like THYLAKOIDS — a stack is called a GRANUM (plural grana). Light reactions (Photosystem I + II, electron transport, ATP synthesis, O₂ evolution) — happen on/in thylakoid membrane. DARK reactions (Calvin cycle, CO₂ fixation) — happen in the stroma. Mitochondrion is for cellular respiration (different organelle). Chloroplasts have their own DNA + ribosomes (semi-autonomous, endosymbiotic origin).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The pigment that absorbs light in BLUE and RED regions and reflects GREEN (giving leaves their colour) is:

options.option_text: Chlorophyll a (with chlorophyll b as accessory)

questions.explanation: Chlorophyll a — the primary photosynthetic pigment; absorbs strongly at ~430 nm (violet-blue) and ~660 nm (red), reflects green ~500-570 nm. Chlorophyll b — accessory pigment; transfers absorbed energy to chl a. Carotenoids (carotene + xanthophyll) — yellow-orange-red; help in light harvesting and protect from photo-oxidation; visible in autumn when chlorophyll degrades. Magnesium is the central metal in the chlorophyll porphyrin ring (Mg²⁺) — in haemoglobin it is iron (Fe²⁺), in vitamin B12 it is cobalt (Co), and in cytochromes it is also iron.

questions.stem: The Calvin cycle (dark reaction) fixes CO₂ using which key enzyme?
questions.explanation: RuBisCO — the most abundant protein on Earth (~50% of soluble leaf protein). Catalyses CO₂ + RuBP (5-C) → 2 × 3-PGA (3-C). It is also a slow and inefficient enzyme — and confuses CO₂ with O₂ when O₂ is high (photorespiration). C₄ plants (maize, sugarcane, sorghum) and CAM plants (cactus, pineapple, agave) evolved CO₂-concentrating mechanisms to bypass photorespiration. Calvin cycle output: 1 net glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate per 3 CO₂; G3P → glucose. Cycle was elucidated by Melvin Calvin (Nobel 1961) using ¹⁴C-tagged CO₂.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The oxygen released in photosynthesis comes from:

options.option_text: Water (H₂O), via photolysis at Photosystem II

questions.explanation: Hill reaction (Robert Hill, 1937) — water is split (photolysis) at PS II: 2H₂O → 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ + O₂. The released O₂ is the byproduct, NOT from CO₂. Verified experimentally with isotope-labelled H₂¹⁸O (Ruben + Kamen, 1941) — the O₂ released bore the ¹⁸O label. Thus 6 CO₂ + 12 H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6 H₂O + 6 O₂ (a more complete equation). Net: 6 CO₂ + 6 H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6 O₂. The Mn-cluster (oxygen-evolving complex) at PS II catalyses water-splitting.

questions.stem: C₄ plants (e.g., maize, sugarcane, sorghum) have an advantage over C₃ plants in hot climates primarily because they:

options.option_text: Concentrate CO₂ around RuBisCO via the Hatch-Slack pathway, minimising photorespiration

questions.explanation: C₄ plants — Hatch-Slack pathway. CO₂ first fixed by PEP-carboxylase in mesophyll cells → 4-carbon oxaloacetate (hence C₄). Transferred to bundle-sheath cells (Kranz anatomy) where CO₂ is released and concentrated around RuBisCO → less O₂ competition → less photorespiration. Adapted to hot, dry, high-light conditions. C₃ plants (rice, wheat, soybean) — direct CO₂ fixation by RuBisCO. CAM plants — open stomata at NIGHT to fix CO₂ as malate; release CO₂ for Calvin cycle by day with stomata closed → conserve water. Examples: cactus, pineapple, agave, orchids.

questions.stem: The MAIN factors limiting the rate of photosynthesis are:

options.option_text: Light intensity, CO₂ concentration, temperature, and water availability

questions.explanation: Blackman's 'law of limiting factors' (1905) — at any moment, the rate is limited by the SLOWEST factor. Key factors: (1) Light intensity — limit at low light; saturates beyond a threshold (light saturation point); (2) CO₂ — current ~420 ppm atmospheric; greenhouses use enrichment (~1000 ppm) to boost growth; (3) Temperature — optimum 25-35 °C; falls steeply above 40 °C (RuBisCO denatures); (4) Water — closes stomata when scarce → limits CO₂ entry. Chlorophyll content + soil minerals (Mg, N, Fe) — long-term factors influencing capacity, not minute-to-minute rate.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Approximately what percentage of the sunlight reaching a leaf is converted to chemical energy (fixed as carbohydrate)?

options.option_text: 1-2% on average (theoretical max ~11%, sugarcane ~6-8% under optimal conditions)

questions.explanation: Photosynthetic efficiency — average crop ~1%, exceptional C₄ crops (sugarcane, maize) ~6-8%. Theoretical max of photosynthesis ~11-12% (limits: only ~50% of solar spectrum is photosynthetically active radiation [PAR, 400-700 nm]; ~5% reflected; ~10% transmitted; energy lost in light reactions, photorespiration, etc.). This low efficiency is a key motivation for synthetic-biology projects to engineer better RuBisCO or transplant C₄ traits into rice (the C₄ Rice Project). Solar PV in contrast — commercial silicon ~22%, lab cells >25%.
